messages:
Kai: heads up — thinking about the console + API flow for 'templated experiments' to speed up A/B canary setup. Main question: should routing rules be exposed as a tiny human DSL or just accept canonical JSON and have the console render an editor? also want per-variant traffic caps + a realtime emergency kill-switch. tradeoffs?

Liz: product POV — start with Quickstart templates (mobile web, search ranking, embeddings rerank) so teams can create experiments in <2 mins. expose an 'Advanced' JSON editor for power users. telemetry toggle should be on by default so evals attach automatically.

Miguel: platform — DSL is nice UX but multiplies parser surface area. prefer one canonical API contract (JSON) and let the console provide a friendly DSL -> JSON transpiler. server-side schema validation + strict guard policies (no negative weights, total target <=1.0). also need a per-experiment immutable id for telemetry. @Kai can we reuse experiment_id from rollout service?

Anya: runtime constraints — whatever we choose, the runtime needs explicit fields for cache keys and KV-prefix sealing so prefix-caching works across variants. also we need a clearly modeled fallback policy: e.g. "fallback: slo_aware" so runtime can pick a cheaper model when latency SLO is at risk.

Ronnie: ops — emergency kill switch must be global and atomic: when toggled it should (a) instantaneously route all traffic to fallback variant, (b) emit an audit event with user id, and (c) page oncall if the toggle was used by non-admin. also add a grace drain option (0s, 30s, 5m). logging/audit important. :rotating_light:

Sam: ml — telemetry shape: every inference should include labels: experiment_id, variant_id, seed_weight, target_traffic. please prefer names that are stable (seed_weight vs initial_weight). for evals we need sample buckets that align with the console's seeding. recommend exposing both seed_weight and target_share.

Miguel: +1 on canonical JSON. quick sample for API v2 payload (simplified):
```json
{
  "experiment_id": "exp_websearch_v3",
  "display_name": "websearch relevance A/B",
  "variants": [
    {"id": "control", "seed_weight": 0.9, "target_share": 0.9, "traffic_cap": 1000},
    {"id": "rerank_v2", "seed_weight": 0.1, "target_share": 0.1, "traffic_cap": 200}
  ],
  "routing_rules": [
    {"if": "user.agent contains 'bot'", "route": "control"},
    {"if": "user.country == 'US'", "route": "split(0.7, 'control','rerank_v2')"}
  ],
  "fallback_policy": "slo_aware",
  "kill_switch_enabled": true
}
```

Miguel: console would show a small DSL editor that maps to the "routing_rules" array above. DSL examples: `country == US -> split(70,control,rerank_v2)` or `is_bot -> control`. keep DSL small and well-documented.

Liz: UX question — in the variant list, should we show both seed_weight and target_share or hide seed_weight behind an "advanced" toggle? my vote: show seed_weight as "initial seeding" with tooltip; show target_share as "intended traffic". keep traffic_cap visible.

Kai: proposal for console implementation: Quickstart templates auto-populate variants + seed_weight. advanced tab exposes JSON and DSL editor. telemetry toggled on, and a prominent "Kill/Abort experiment" button with 2-step confirm. question: UI label for variant quota — use "traffic_cap (qps)" or "max_qps"? thoughts?

Ronnie: prefer "max_qps" — clearer for SREs. also we should surface runtime-estimated breach risk (if projected QPS > capacity) in the draft view.

Sam: +1 to showing both seed and target. also ask backend to emit a preflight simulation result (expected p50/p95 and token cost delta) when you create a new variant. helps product teams decide on traffic caps.

Anya: runtime needs explicit fields for preflight hints: expected_latency_ms, estimated_token_cost. add these to the create API response from simulation.

Kai: ok actionable items: (1) Miguel will draft canonical JSON schema for API v2 (include audit fields, kill_switch, fallback_policy, telemetry flags) — due EOD Fri. (2) Liz will mock Quickstart templates + advanced editor UX. (3) Anya + Ronnie will spec kill-switch behavior and paging rules. (4) Sam will write telemetry label contract.

Miguel: noted. I'll open API PR and include server-side validation rules and an example DSL->JSON transpiler module. linking internal doc: http://go/redwood/rollouts-console-guidelines :eyes:

deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled: api-rollouts/v2 -> canary/us-east at 2026-03-21T09:00Z :rocket:

Kai: thanks all — let's sync in the experiment sync tomorrow. if anyone wants to weight-in on the DSL size vs features, drop comments on the PR. :thumbsup:
